summary: AWS SSO session-duration policy change causing external operator sessions to expire mid-provision and breaking dedicated capacity onboarding
description: Summary: After an org-level change to AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) default session duration on 2026-03-09, external operators intermittently lose credentials while performing Dedicated provisioning workflows. Impact: several dedicated onboarding runs failed between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-12 with STS assume/refresh errors; provisioning of new GPU pools delayed ~20-40 minutes for affected customers. Scope: observed in prod-us-east for external operator principals that authenticate via SSO and then call our dedicated-provisioner service which assumes roles into customer-linked accounts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login via AWS SSO (external operator account) and obtain temporary session (okta -> SSO) with permission-set A
2) Trigger dedicated provisioner job to create reserved capacity in customer account (calls AssumeRole in target account with DurationSeconds=3600),
3) Observe that token used by provisioner is rejected by STS or expires earlier than DurationSeconds resulting in access denied or token-expired errors mid-run
4) Re-run after re-authenticating via SSO and sometimes job completes if reauth gives a fresh session - but failures are nondeterministic and cluster around the recent org policy change
logs: 2026-03-11T01:12:23Z provisioner ERROR assume-role failed: STS AssumeRoleFailure RequestId=abc123efg region=us-east-1 error=ExpiredToken: The security token included in the request is expired
CloudTrail snippet: eventTime=2026-03-11T01:11:58Z eventName=AssumeRole awsRegion=us-east-1 userIdentity.type=AssumedRole sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName=external-ops@example.com
SSO audit: 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC: org-config changed: default session duration from 12h -> 1h (admin: infra-org-owner@example.com)
comments: Asha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed three separate dedicated onboarding failures this morning. Correlated with SSO session renewals. Opening ticket to track root cause and mitigation.

Liam O'Connor (assignee) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by setting SSO session to 1h then starting provisioner job. Provisioner requests a longer DurationSeconds (3600) but underlying SSO session lifetime can be shorter when SSO issues a shorter source session -> token chain breaks. Investigating codepath that sets requested DurationSeconds.

SRE (Maya Ruiz) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed CloudTrail shows STS responses with ExpiredToken at ~55-60 minutes after initial auth, consistent with session duration change. Quick mitigation: advise operators to re-auth before long-running jobs; planning infra change to cap DurationSeconds requested by provisioner.

Infra Owner (Samir Khanna) - 2026-03-13: Reverted org default session-duration to 8h for external operator permission-sets while we deploy code fix. Noted as temporary; will follow up with policy that prevents unexpected org-wide session overrides without change control.
Liam O'Connor - 2026-03-14: Deployed fix in infra repo to cap requested role DurationSeconds to min(source_session, 3600) and added retries on AssumeRole failure. Monitoring for regressions.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Org-level SSO session-duration reduction causes source SSO session to be shorter than DurationSeconds requested by our AssumeRole chain, causing STS to return ExpiredToken during a long-running workflow.
Hypothesis 2: Some permission-sets are still attached to legacy session-duration profiles; provisioning path does not validate source session expiry before requesting long-lived downstream creds.
Evidence: CloudTrail and SSO audit records show session-duration change on 2026-03-09. STS errors cluster ~55-65 minutes after operator login. Reproduced by setting SSO session to 1h in test account.
Root cause: Combination of (a) sudden org-level session-duration reduction, and (b) provisioner requesting DurationSeconds without verifying the operator's source session remaining lifetime.
resolution: Mitigation implemented 2026-03-13: org-session-duration for affected permission-sets temporarily restored to 8h to stop ongoing customer-impact while code fix rolled out. Fix deployed 2026-03-14: provisioner now caps requested DurationSeconds to the source session remaining lifetime and to a safe max (3600s) and retries on ExpiredToken with exponential backoff. Follow-ups: create infra-as-code guardrail PR to require change-control for org SSO session-duration (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5432), add dashboard alert for STS ExpiredToken spikes, and update runbook with steps to detect and mitigate SSO session policy changes. Ticket remains In Progress until monitoring confirms no regressions for 72h.
next_steps: 1) Monitoring: watch STS ExpiredToken metric and oncall alert threshold for 72 hours (owner: SRE)
2) Documentation: update Dedicated runbook to include SSO session-duration mismatch checks (owner: Docs)
3) Policy: submit change-control proposal to lock default org session-duration changes (owner: Security/Infra)
4) Postmortem: if more than 5 customer-onboard failures occurred due to this, trigger a short postmortem (owner: Support)
5) Close ticket when monitoring clears (72h) and guardrail PR merged
